newsitem.title: USA: US West Media, Airtouch merge wireless.
newsitem.headline: US West Media, Airtouch merge wireless.

text.p: U S WEST Media Group said it would merge its domestic cellular business NewVector and its interest in PrimeCo Personal Communications into AirTouch Communications in a deal valued at about $5 billion.

As a result of the deal, AirTouch said it would obtain ownership of Media Group's domestic wireless business. The transaction included AirTouch's assumption of $2.2 billion of debt and the distribution of AirTouch stock to Media Group shareholders tax-free, the companies said.

AirTouch said it expected to add to its proportionate U.S. cellular and PCS portfolio up to about 34 million POPs, 1.9 million customers and $300 million operating cash flow, based on pro-forma 1996 results.
This would bring its worldwide proportionate totals to 212 million POPS, 10 million customers and $1.4 billion operating cash flow, the company said.
U S Media Group's overseas wireless properties were not affected, it said.
The deal was seen as $0.30 per share dilutive to AirTouch's earnings in the first full year, with that sum delining from then on, the company said.
It would be accretive to cash-flow, AirTouch said.
Under terms of the deal, the number of AirTouch shares issued would vary depending on the trading price of AirTouch stock, U S West Media said.

AirTouch would issue 84.8 million shares to Media Group shareholders if AirTouch stock was trading at $33 or higher, the company said. But if AirTouch was trading at $30 or lower, Media Group would get 93.3 million AirTouch shares, it said.
AirTouch stock closed at 23-1/2 on Thursday, off 1/4 while U S Media Group's stock also finished off 1/4 at 17-1/4.
AirTouch said it expected to maintain its investment grade rating.

Under the transaction, which the companies said would be tax-free, U S WEST would distribute shares of a newly formed company consisting all of its businesses other than the Media Group's domestic wireless businesses to shareholders, the company said.

It would then merge the remaining domestic wireless businesses with AirTouch or an AirTouch unit via in a deal in which AirTouch common shares would be distributed directly to holders of U S WEST Media Group common stock, it said.
The companies said they expected the deal to close by the end of the year but said the "Morris Trust" legislation introduced in Congress would block the deal if it passed in its current form.
If this happened, the companies said they would continue their joint venture in its current form.

The ability to include in the transaction certain of U S West's cellular interests representing four million to five milion POPs could be dependent on the outcome of pending litigation or the receipt of third-party consents, it said.

If the deal was consummated, it would replace 1994 agreements between AirTouch and U S West which called for the companies to combine their U.S. cellular operations and interests in PrimeCo in a multi-phased deal, they said.
Because Media Group's cellular operations began using the AirTouch brand about a year ago, those customers would not be affected by the change, the companies said.
In addition, Media Group's domestic cellular employees would generally follow their work and become AirTouch employees once the transaction is final, they said.
The transaction would require a definitive agreement and various shareholder and regulatory approvals, they said.
Media Group, a broadband communications company, is one of two major groups that make up U S West, the other being U S West Communications. AirTouch is a global wireless communications company.
